n: Igreja Matriz de Nossa Senhora do Pilar (Ouro Preto)
w: One of the best-known churches raised during Brazil's Gold Rush, this basilica on Monsenhor Castilho Barbosa Square carries minor-basilica status and IPHAN heritage listing. Locally it is shortened to the Mother Church -- Ouro Preto's principal parish among the town's cluster of baroque gold-money churches.
s: A Gold Rush basilica on Monsenhor Castilho Barbosa Square
_facts: Minor basilica dedicated to Our Lady of the Pillar
Built during the Brazilian Gold Rush
Listed monument by IPHAN
Located at Monsenhor Castilho Barbosa Square

w: Brazil's failed 1789 independence plot, the Inconfidencia Mineira, gets its museum inside a former jail on Tiradentes Square, named for the executed conspirator. Established in 1938 and declared a National Museum of Brazil in 1990, it holds relics of rebels who died for a Brazil that came only decades later.
s: A failed 1789 rebellion's museum, inside its old jail
_facts: History museum on the failed Inconfidencia Mineira independence movement
Housed in a former jail on Tiradentes Square
Established 1938
Declared a National Museum of Brazil in 1990

n: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary
w: Built by and for Ouro Preto's enslaved and free Black population, this IPHAN-landmarked church stands out as one of the most architecturally original colonial-era sacred buildings anywhere in Brazil, its curved facade breaking away from the town's more conventional baroque church fronts.
s: A colonial church built by Ouro Preto's Black community
_facts: Catholic church built for the Black community during the colonial period
Landmarked by IPHAN
Noted as an architecturally original colonial sacred building

n: Church of Saint Francis of Assisi (Ouro Preto)
w: Antonio Francisco Lisboa -- Aleijadinho, the disabled sculptor-architect -- designed both the structure and every carved decoration here, begun in 1766 after a 19-year wait for Lisbon's approval. Its circular bell towers and relief oculus were unheard of in Brazilian church design.
s: Aleijadinho's Rococo masterpiece, 19 years in permitting
_facts: Designed by Antonio Francisco Lisboa (Aleijadinho), construction begun 1766
Circular bell towers and oculus, novel for the period
Ceiling painting by Manuel da Costa Ataide
UNESCO World Heritage listed; one of Brazil's Seven Wonders

w: Heritage body SPHAN wanted a modern hotel dropped into Brazil's best-preserved baroque gold town, and in 1940 picked a young Oscar Niemeyer's design over rival Carlos Leao's -- one of Niemeyer's earliest works, decades before Brasilia. It still stands as a concrete outlier among Ouro Preto's colonial church towers.
s: Niemeyer's first hotel, dropped into a baroque gold town
_facts: Built 1940, one of Oscar Niemeyer's early works
Commissioned by heritage body SPHAN, in consultation with Lucio Costa
Niemeyer's design chosen over Carlos Leao's
Sits within Ouro Preto's historic baroque townscape

w: This Church of Our Lady of Mount Carmel counts among Brazil's finer examples of Rococo religious architecture, its IPHAN listing recognising a baroque tradition that turned Ouro Preto's gold-mining wealth into carved stone and gilded altars across an entire hill town of churches.
s: A Rococo landmark from Ouro Preto's gold-money churches
_facts: Catholic church in the Rococo architectural tradition
Listed monument by IPHAN (National Institute of Historic and Artistic Heritage)
